A reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) changes how radio signals are reflected and thereby affects the radio channel. We model these channels, develop surface control algorithms and test them on experimental prototypes.

RIS research began in 2023 as an initiative by laboratory staff and students. Fourth-year students carried out the first studies, modeling basic RIS application scenarios for their graduation theses.

The work continued through a project at the TUSUR Advanced Engineering School. Support from the UMNIK competition enabled the team to move from modeling to building prototypes. Surfaces with [16](#ris-prototype) and [64 elements](#ris-exhibition) have been designed and manufactured.

For the 16-element surface, the team developed a controller and software for configuring the RIS and evaluating its operation in real time. A mobile phone control module is also under development. For [anechoic chamber measurements](#ris-chamber), students built a [stepper-motor rotation device with indicator lights](#ris-control).

Two graduates who started working on RIS as students continued this work in postgraduate research. We study surface control algorithms, remote control from mobile devices and RIS applications in non-terrestrial networks. Another topic is STAR-RIS: surfaces that simultaneously reflect and transmit electromagnetic waves.

The work involves microwave modeling, antenna engineering, mechanical design, PCB layout, controller development and radio measurements. Results have been presented in scientific publications, at EDM conferences and technical exhibitions, including [Rost UP](#ris-exhibition), and in students’ graduation theses.

This research combines modeling and algorithm development, refinement of prototypes and measurement methods, and training students in research and engineering.
